paras.en: So the seventh planet was Earth.
paras.zh: 于是，第七颗行星就是地球。

paras.en: Earth is no ordinary planet! It has one hundred and eleven kings (not forgetting, of course, the black kings), seven thousand geographers, nine hundred thousand businessmen, seven and a half million drunkards, three hundred and eleven million conceited men—in other words, about two billion grown-ups.
paras.zh: 地球可不是一颗普通的行星！那里有一百一十一位国王（当然，也没有忘记黑人国王）、七千位地理学家、九十万商人、七百五十万酒鬼、三亿一千一百万个爱虚荣的人，也就是说，大人们大约有二十亿。

paras.en: To give you an idea of the size of Earth, I will tell you that before electricity was invented, a whole army of four hundred and sixty-two thousand five hundred and eleven lamplighters had to be maintained across all six continents.
paras.zh: 为了让你们知道地球有多大，我要告诉你们，在电被发明出来以前，地球的六块大陆上得养着四十六万二千五百一十一名点灯人，真是一支大军。

paras.en: Seen from a little way off, it was a splendid sight. The movements of this army were timed like those of a ballet at the opera. First came the turn of the lamplighters in New Zealand and Australia. Then, once they had lit their little lamps, they went off to sleep. Then the lamplighters in China and Siberia took their turn in the dance. Then they too vanished into the wings. Then came the turn of the lamplighters in Russia and the Indies. Then those in Africa and Europe. Then those in South America. Then those in North America. And they never got the order of their entrances wrong. It was magnificent.
paras.zh: 从稍远一点的地方看，那景象美极了。这支大军的动作，就像歌剧里的芭蕾舞一样，安排得井井有条。先轮到新西兰和澳大利亚的点灯人。然后，他们点亮自己的小灯，就去睡觉了。接着，中国和西伯利亚的点灯人也轮到上场跳舞了。然后，他们也一闪身，消失在侧幕里。接着轮到俄罗斯和印度的点灯人。然后是非洲和欧洲的。然后是南美洲的。然后是北美洲的。他们从来不把出场的次序弄错。真是壮观。

paras.en: Only the lamplighter who tended the single streetlamp at the North Pole, and his fellow lamplighter who tended the single streetlamp at the South Pole, led idle, carefree lives: they worked twice a year.
paras.zh: 只有照管北极那唯一一盏路灯的点灯人，和他那照管南极唯一一盏路灯的同行，过着闲散悠然的日子：他们每年工作两次。
